artworks.title: Hercules and Omphale
artworks.description: Cranach's exchange of genders — Heracles at Omphale's spindle, the Lydian year of soft bondage between Troy and the later labours.

artworks.title: Hercules at the Feet of Omphale (Hercule aux pieds d'Omphale)
artworks.description: Dantan's Salon canvas — the hero at the queen's feet, club and lion-skin surrendered for the spindle.

artworks.title: Drunken Hercules and Queen Omphale (Pompeian fresco)
artworks.description: Pompeian fresco — drunken Hercules and Omphale, Roman domestic myth of the hero unarmed.

artworks.title: Omphale and Hercules (fresco tondo)
artworks.description: Fresco tondo of Omphale and Hercules — the Lydian queen still holding the hero who sacked Laomedon's Troy.

popCulture.title: Omphale
popCulture.description: The Lydian queen who held Heracles in soft bondage — the hero's servitude between the sack of Laomedon's Troy and his later labours.

popCulture.title: Heracles
popCulture.description: The first sack of Ilion and the year of Omphale's spindle — Heracles' Trojan prelude before Priam's city fell to the Achaeans.
